Report_ID: Smoking abstinence at 12 months (repeated point abstinence at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months post-cessation, ITT)
Title: Happy Ending: a randomized controlled trial of a digital multi-media smoking cessation intervention
Author: Brendryen & Kraft
Comment: Paper reports an odds ratio, not a risk ratio; RR must be computed downstream from the extracted 2x2 counts (44/197 vs 26/199). Abstinence self-reported only.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Happy Ending digital multi-media intervention (internet + cell-phone) plus free NRT') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Medium: internet (e-mail, web pages) and cell-phone (SMS, interactive voice response)
Participant type: adult smokers (>=18 years, >=10 cigarettes/day) motivated to quit
Outcome measurement: self-reported 7-day abstinence assessed via internet surveys or telephone interviews; no biochemical validation
Outcome variable: Smoking abstinence at 12 months (repeated point abstinence at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months post-cessation, ITT)
outcome_family: smoking cessation (abstinence) at 6 months or longer

Report_ID: 6-month sustained abstinence at 7 months (missing coded as smoker) - QuitCoach only vs minimal-information control
Title: Population-level effects of automated smoking cessation help programs: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Borland, Balmford & Benda
Comment: Raw event counts are not reported; only per-arm percentages with denominators and odds ratios. No biochemical validation. Overlaps with the 'all interventions combined vs control' comparison (same control arm) - use only one in a pooled analysis.
Participant type: adult smokers and recent quitters interested in quitting (mean age 42.1 years, 60% female)
Recruitment source: Quitline information-seekers (n = 1335) and cold-contacted internet survey panels (n = 2195)
Outcome measurement: Self-report of not smoking for 6 months sustained at 7-month follow-up
Outcome variable: 6-month sustained abstinence at 7 months (missing coded as smoker) - QuitCoach only vs minimal-information control
outcome_family: smoking cessation (abstinence) at 6 months or longer

Report_ID: Repeated point abstinence at 12 months (abstinence at 1 + 3 + 6 + 12 months)
Title: A Digital Smoking Cessation Program Delivered Through Internet and Cell Phone Without Nicotine Replacement (Happy Ending): Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Brendryen, Drozd, Kraft
Comment: Abstinence self-reported without biochemical verification. Odds ratio (not risk ratio) is the paper's own reported measure; raw event counts and ITT denominators are provided so an RR can be computed downstream. NRT use was higher in the intervention arm; an NRT-adjusted OR of 2.86 (95% CI 1.31-6.24, P=.008) is also reported but the unadjusted ITT result is extracted as the primary comparison.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Happy Ending (HE) digital multimedia intervention') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Medium: Internet (email, tailored Web pages) plus cell phone (IVR, SMS)
Participant type: adult daily smokers (>=18 years, >=5 cigarettes/day) willing to quit without nicotine replacement therapy
Recruitment source: Online banner advertisements in Norwegian regional newspapers
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of abstainers out of participants randomised in each arm
Outcome variable: Repeated point abstinence at 12 months (abstinence at 1 + 3 + 6 + 12 months)
outcome_family: smoking cessation (abstinence) at 6 months or longer

Title: Internet-Based Photoaging Within Australian Pharmacies to Promote Smoking Cessation: Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Burford O, Jiwa M, Carter O, Parsons R, Hendrie D
Comment: Paper does not report a risk ratio or odds ratio; only counts, percentages with CIs, chi-square and adjusted logistic-regression P values (adjusted P=.03 for confirmed quitting) are given. Control-arm CO validation uptake was low (only 1 of 5 self-reported quitters consented), which the authors note may bias the CO-validated comparison. Self-reported quitting (5/80 vs 22/80, P<.001) was the same construct in the same study and was deduplicated in favour of the more rigorous CO-validated endpoint.
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (between-subjects, unblinded, alternate-week allocation by pharmacy)
Medium: Internet-based 3-D age-progression software (APRIL Face Aging v2.5) delivered by pharmacist, aged photo emailed within 24 hours
Topic of Content: Personalized photoaging images showing facial effects of lifelong smoking versus nonsmoking
Participant type: Young adult smokers aged 18-30 years smoking ≥1 cigarette/day, not using NRT or oral cessation drugs
Recruitment source: 8 metropolitan community pharmacies around Perth city centre, Western Australia
Outcome measurement: Number of confirmed nonsmokers out of 80 randomised per arm at 6 months
outcome_family: smoking cessation (abstinence) at 6 months or longer

Report_ID: Prolonged abstinence at 12 months (MTC vs. usual care)
Title: Results of the PAS Study: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Web-Based Multiple Tailored Smoking Cessation Program Combined With Tailored Counseling by Practice Nurses
Author: E. S. Smit, M. J. J. M. Candel, C. Hoving, H. de Vries
Comment: Event counts and denominators are from the available-data (followed-up) samples at 12 months (MTC n = 93 of 163 randomized; UC n = 64 of 119 randomized), not intention-to-treat denominators; the paper states a negative-scenario sensitivity analysis (dropouts counted as smokers) "yielded similar results" but does not report those arm-level counts or ORs. The reported OR comes from a logistic multilevel model (available data, covariate-adjusted where covariates were retained), so it is not a crude 2x2 estimate. No risk ratio is reported by the paper. Cotinine-validated abstinence rates by arm are not reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('MTC: Web-based multiple computer tailoring + face-to-face practice nurse counseling + 6-month telephone call') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: primary care / general practice, with online intervention delivery
Medium: Internet (web-based computer-tailored feedback) plus face-to-face and telephone counseling
Participant type: Dutch adult smokers motivated to quit within 6 months, recruited in general practice
Recruitment source: 91 practice nurses in Dutch general practices, May 2009 to June 2010
Outcome measurement: Number of respondents reporting prolonged abstinence out of respondents followed up at 12 months per arm
Outcome variable: Prolonged abstinence at 12 months (MTC vs. usual care)
outcome_family: smoking cessation (abstinence) at 6 months or longer
